items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen after dinner. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes seems to be enough to get most of the benefit, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Try not to eat dinner too late, as sugar tends to rise more after late dinners, about 9.2 mg/dL more. None of your scored dinners were late, so keep up the good habit.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You're doing great with your overnight fast, averaging 15.5 hours and always reaching at least 13 hours. This habit is part of your coaching and may have some benefits, but more research is needed to understand its effects.
